addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- agentsight-insight-artifact: Generate Claude-Insights-style AgentSight summaries and shareable single-file HTML artifacts from AgentSight snapshot JSON, record SQLite databases, monitor SQLite databases under ~/.agentsight/monitor, or active/local AgentSight data. Use when the user asks to create AgentSight insights, artifact reports, shareable investigation pages, monitor summaries, usage summaries, failure/resource findings, or Claude Code artifact-like reports for AgentSight traces.
- audit-paper-consistency: Audits selected LaTeX or prose for consistency with the rest of a systems paper—architecture, terminology, claims, figures/tables/listings, interfaces vs mechanisms, workflows, and notation. Use when checking cross-section alignment, naming drift, contradictions with artifacts, or unsupported claims introduced in a passage; complements critique and targeted-fix skills.
- auto-research-orchestrator: Orchestrate or resume a research project from idea to paper submission. Use when the user asks what research stage they are in, what gate blocks progress, how to resume after context loss, what the next research action is, or which specialist workflow should run next. Applies across systems, ML, agents, measurement, infrastructure, and empirical research. Do not use for standalone prose editing, a single experiment-design request, a one-off literature summary, or ordinary paper review unless the user asks for lifecycle routing or gate decisions.
- critique-like-senior-systems-reviewer: Critiques a selected LaTeX section as a skeptical senior SOSP/OSDI reviewer, separating writing vs logic vs technical vs evidence gaps, ranking severity, and giving concrete fixes. Use when the user asks for a systems-style critique, reviewer simulation, section review, or "OSDI/SOSP reviewer" feedback on introduction, design, evaluation, related work, or any subsection.
- kvm-benchmark-workflow: Run or audit KVM/QEMU/virtme-ng benchmark workflows for systems research. Use when executing VM-backed benchmarks, interpreting KVM numbers for a paper, debugging local KVM benchmark setup, checking benchmark Makefile targets, or validating result provenance and baseline parity. Do not use for generic builds unrelated to VM execution, cloud-only benchmark runs, or prose-only paper review.
- oss-change-workflow: Maintainer-quality workflow for implementing open-source feature requests, bug fixes, regressions, compatibility fixes, documentation-linked code changes, or issue-backed patches. Use when changing code in an OSS repository and the task needs scope control, reproduction, tests, docs/changelog sync, maturity-aware commit/push or PR handoff, independent AI review for mature projects, and CI closure when applicable. Do not use for issue triage without code changes, release preparation, or standalone GitHub CI debugging.
- oss-issue-triage: Triage open-source GitHub issues and maintainer inbox items. Use when classifying issues, drafting maintainer replies, deciding labels/priority/milestones, requesting reproduction details, finding duplicates, deciding close/reopen/escalate, or separating bug, feature, support, docs, and security reports. Do not use when the user asks to implement the fix, prepare a release, or debug CI.
- oss-release-readiness: Audit or prepare an open-source release. Use when checking whether a repo is ready to tag, publish, cut a GitHub release, update changelog/release notes, bump versions, publish packages, document breaking changes, or verify release smoke tests and provenance. Do not use for ordinary feature/bug implementation, issue triage, or paper prose review.
- paper-writing-style: Review and fix academic writing in LaTeX paper sections. Checks terminology, sentence structure, word choice, and systems-paper conventions. NEVER rewrite — only supplement and make minimal targeted changes. - Review paper writing, fix academic prose, check terminology consistency, find writing antipatterns, polish prose
- project-bootstrap-workflow: Bootstrap a lean new project, repository, research prototype, tutorial, demo, paper artifact, OSS library, CLI/tooling repo, or small web/app project. Use when creating a fresh project directory, choosing initial structure, initializing git/GitHub, writing the first README, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, package/build files, smoke test, or first runnable example. Emphasizes minimal files, main/master direct-push for immature projects, and avoiding premature CI, release, multi-agent, or production scaffolding. Do not use for ordinary feature changes in an existing repo, release preparation, or CI debugging.
- research-experiment-design: Design or audit top-conference research experiments for systems, ML, measurement, agents, infrastructure, and empirical research. Use when planning a paper evaluation, mapping claims to experiments, choosing baselines/metrics/workloads/datasets, designing ablations, scalability, fault-injection, robustness, statistical validity checks, benchmark methodology, experiment run order, or checking whether results are strong enough for venues such as OSDI/SOSP/NSDI/EuroSys/ICML/NeurIPS/ICLR/SIGMETRICS.
- research-literature-novelty: Build a claim-oriented literature and novelty map for a research project. Use when searching related work, checking closest prior work, identifying same-claim risk, choosing baselines, summarizing papers for a top-conference framing, downloading/organizing reference PDFs, or updating docs/background-related-work.md. Applies across systems, ML, agents, measurement, infrastructure, and empirical research. Persistent narrative output, when allowed, must go only to docs/background-related-work.md plus optional docs/tmp/phase-1-related-work dated notes; requested raw reference PDFs may go under docs/reference/.
- research-project-startup: Frame an early-stage research project into a top-conference-ready idea story. Use when starting or resuming a research idea, turning rough notes into a scoped problem/story/claim set, deciding whether an idea is paper-shaped, or updating docs/idea-story.md. Applies across systems, ML, agents, measurement, infrastructure, and empirical research. Persistent output, when allowed, must go only to docs/idea-story.md plus optional docs/tmp/phase-0-framing dated notes.
- resolve-shepherd-reviewer-comment: Revises selected LaTeX to address a specific shepherd or reviewer concern with minimal churn, explicit traceability to the comment, and conservative claims. Use when the user pastes a review comment, quotes reviewer/shepherd text, asks to fix a specific concern, or wants a targeted revision rather than a full section rewrite.
- revise-section-sosp-osdi: Revise a LaTeX section in the style of a strong SOSP/OSDI systems paper, improving top-down narrative flow, mechanism clarity, and reviewer readability while preserving technical meaning. Use when the user asks to revise, rewrite, tighten, restructure, or improve a section, subsection, or paragraph of a systems paper, especially during shepherding or camera-ready revision.
- tech-blog-writer: Write or improve systems/infrastructure blog posts for developer audiences. This skill should be used when writing a tech blog about eBPF, observability, AI agents, kernel internals, performance, or infrastructure topics. Also applies to converting notes/papers into blog format, improving prose in existing posts, or writing EN/ZH bilingual blog pairs. Examples: "write a blog about X", "draft a post on Y", "improve this post", "turn these notes into a blog", "write up this work", "help me with the blog draft".
- tighten-prose-systems-latex: Tightens selected LaTeX prose for SOSP/OSDI-style systems papers by cutting redundancy and vague wording while preserving mechanisms, qualifiers, and evidence. Use when the user asks to tighten, shorten, de-verbose, or polish LaTeX without changing technical claims, or when prose feels wordy but the structure is acceptable.
- agent-behavior-artifact: Create shareable Markdown, PR comments, incident briefs, dashboard-like summaries, or single-file HTML artifacts from AI agent behavior facts, session inventories, friction findings, local Claude/Codex/Gemini logs, AgentSight snapshots or monitor DBs, OpenTelemetry GenAI JSON/span exports, LangSmith run JSON, Langfuse trace exports, or Datadog MCP query results. Use when the user asks for an artifact, investigation report, team brief, reviewer note, or Claude Code Insights-style page about AI agent behavior.
- agent-friction-analysis: Diagnose friction in AI agent sessions from session inventories, tool traces, local Claude/Codex/Gemini logs, AgentSight audit rows or monitor DBs, OpenTelemetry GenAI spans, LangSmith run JSON, Langfuse trace exports, Datadog LLM Observability MCP query results, or plain transcripts. Use when the user asks why an agent struggled, repeated work, failed tools/tests, retried commands, got interrupted, wasted tokens, left side effects, contradicted its summary, or needs CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/tooling improvements.
- agent-session-inventory: Summarize AI coding-agent session histories from local Claude Code/Codex/Gemini logs, Claude usage-data, AgentSight snapshots or monitor DBs, OpenTelemetry GenAI JSON/span exports, LangSmith run JSON, Langfuse trace exports, Datadog MCP query results, or plain session logs. Use when the user asks for recent agent usage, project/session inventory, active projects, model/tool/token/cost distribution, session coverage, or evidence availability; do not use for root-cause diagnosis or shareable artifacts.
- blog-review: Review and fix prose style in the specified blog post file. If no file is given, ask which file t...
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
有两个 submodule：

1. **libbpf** — `https://github.com/libbpf/libbpf.git`
2. **bpftool** — `https://github.com/libbpf/bpftool.git`

两个都是 eBPF 相关的依赖库，当前状态前面带 `-` 表示还没有初始化（未 `git submodule update --init`）。
